chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Jameel, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him); and Hammad ibn Uthman, from Al-Halabi, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him).
He said: If the gift remains exactly as it was (in its original state), then he has the right to retract it; otherwise, he does not have the right.

key_terms.قَائِمَةً بِعَيْنِهَا: Remaining in its original state/exact form

ai.seo_question: Can a donor take back a gift in Shia Islamic law?
ai.summary: This hadith, transmitted through the prominent chain of al-Kulayni, clarifies the condition of 'qiyam bi-al-ayn' (remaining in the donor's possession) as the decisive factor for revoking a gift (hibah) in Shia jurisprudence. It underscores the principle that once the gift is fully transferred and altered or consumed by the recipient, the donor loses the right of return, a ruling consistent with the majority of Shia jurists (fuqaha). This distinction highlights the legal finality of the gift contract upon effective delivery and acceptance.
